verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              किं तस्यां मम सेनायां नासन्केचिन्महारथाः। ये तथा सात्यकिं यान्तं नैवाघ्नन्नाप्यवारयन् ॥१॥
एको हि समरे कर्म कृतवान् सत्यविक्रमः। शक्रतुल्यबलो युद्धे महेन्द्रो दानवेष्विव ॥२॥
verses.english: Of indomitable prowess and possessed of strength equal to that of Indra himself, singlehanded he achieved feats amidst my troops like Indra achieving feats amidst the Danavas.

verses.sanskrit: अथवा शून्यमासीत्तद्येन यातः स सात्यकिः। हतभूयिष्ठमथवा येन यातः स सात्यकिः ॥३॥
verses.english: Perhaps the track through which Satyaki passed was empty. Possessed of prowess in the true sense of the term, he alone has crushed numerous hosts, of mine.

verses.sanskrit: यत्कृतं वृष्णिवीरेण कर्म शंससि मे रणे। नैतदुत्सहते कर्तुं कर्म शक्रोऽपि संजय ॥४॥
अश्रद्धेयमचिन्त्यं च कर्म तस्य महात्मनः। वृष्ण्यन्धकप्रवीरस्य श्रुत्वा मे व्यथितं मनः ॥५॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said O monarch, the exertion and din that were then made by your troops, O king, teeming with cars, elephants, foot-soldiers, resembled that which occurs at the end of a Yuga.

verses.sanskrit: न सन्ति तस्मात् पुत्रा मे यथा सञ्जय भाषसे। एको वै बहुलाः सेनाः प्रामृद्नात सत्यविक्रमः ॥६॥
कथं च युध्यमानानामपक्रान्तो महात्मनाम्। एको बहूनां शैनेयस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व सञ्जय ॥७॥
verses.english: The Gods and the Charanas that then came there said, "this muster will be the last of its kind on the earth."

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              राजन्सेनासमुद्योगो रथनागाश्वपत्तिमान्। तुमुलस्तव सैन्यानां युगान्तसदृशोऽभवत् ॥८॥
आहूतेषु समूहेषु तव सैन्यस्य मानद। नाभूल्लोके समः कश्चित्समूह इति मे मतिः ॥९॥
verses.english: Then the din that was made by the armies as they rushed to battle with one another, was as tremendous as one created by the ocean agitated with the vehemence of a mighty tempest.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र देवास्त्वभाषन्त चारणाश्च समागताः। एतदन्ताः समूहा वै भविष्यन्ति महीतले ॥१०॥
verses.english: In those two assembled hosts of the Pandavas and the Kurus, O foremost of men,

verses.sanskrit: न च वै तादृशो व्यूह आसीत्कश्चिद्विशांपते। यादृग्जयद्रथवधे द्रोणेन विहितोऽभवत् ॥११॥
चण्डवातविभिन्नानां समुद्राणामिव स्वनः। रणेऽभवद्बलौघानामन्योन्यमभिधावताम् ॥१२॥
पार्थिवानां समेतानां बहून्यासन्नरोत्तम। त्वद्बले पाण्डवानां च सह‌स्राणि शतानि च ॥१३॥
संरब्धानां प्रवीराणां समरे दृढकर्मणाम्। तत्रासीत्सुमहाशब्दस्तुमुलो लोमहर्षणः ॥१४॥
verses.english: Do you so act, as they may proceed easily towards the chariot of Jayadratha. Speaking thus, they urged their troops on.

verses.sanskrit: अथाक्रन्दद्भीमसेनो धृष्टद्युम्नश्च मारिष। नकुलः सहदेवश्च धर्मराजश्च पाण्डवः ॥१५॥
verses.english: (They again said)-"If those two heroes be slain, then the Kurus will have their objects fulfilled and we shall be defeated. Therefore do you united exert yourselves for agitating this host, like the tempest of tremendous vehemence agitating the ocean. O king, urged on by the Panchala prince and by Bhimasena.

verses.sanskrit: आगच्छत प्रहरत द्रुतं विपरिधावत। प्रविष्टावरिसेनां हि वीरौ माधवपाण्डवौ ॥१६॥
verses.english: And king Vasudana began to shout loudly amidst the Pandava troops. 'Come, strike, rush upon the foe quickly.

verses.sanskrit: यथा सुखेन गच्छेतां जयद्रथवधं प्रति। तथा प्रकुरुत क्षिप्रमिति सैन्यान्यचोदयन् ॥१७॥
तयोरभावे कुरवः कृतार्थाः स्युर्वयं जिताः। ते यूयं सहिता भूत्वा तूर्णमेव बलार्णवम् ॥१८॥
verses.english: They fell to slaughter the Kurus thoroughly disregarding their own dear lives. Possessed of i great energy, all of them desiring death in

verses.sanskrit: क्षोभयध्वं महावेगाः पवनः सागरं यथा। भीमसेनेन ते राजन्पाञ्चाल्येन च नोदिताः ॥१९॥
आजघ्नुः कौरवान्सङ्ख्ये त्यक्त्वाऽसूनात्मनः प्रियान्। इच्छन्तो निधनं युद्धे शस्त्रैरुत्तमतेजसः ॥२०॥
verses.english: And setting their hearts resolutely on battle, remained on the field, determined to to fight to the bitter end. In that dreadful and horible battle.

verses.sanskrit: स्वर्गेप्सवो मित्रकार्ये नाभ्यनन्दन्त जीवितम्। तथैव तावका राजन्प्रार्थयन्तो महद्यशः ॥२१॥
आर्यां युद्धे मतिं कृत्वा युद्धायैवावतस्थिरे। तस्मिन्सुतुमुले युद्धे वर्तमाने भयावहे ॥२२॥
verses.english: Satyaki having vanquished all the warriors advanded towards Arjuna. The combatants were compelled to turn their eyes away from the coats of mails covering the warriors, as the reflected the rays of the sun directly. O monarch, Duryodhana then penetrated through the mighty host of the illustrious sons of Pandu striving hard in battle. Then the battle that was there fought between him and them was extremely terrible and the carnage horrible.

verses.sanskrit: जित्वा सर्वाणि सैन्यानि प्रायात्सात्यकिरर्जुनम्। कवचानां प्रभास्तत्र सूर्यरश्मिविराजिताः ॥२३॥
दृष्टीः सङ्ख्ये सैनिकानां प्रतिजघ्नुः समन्ततः। तथा प्रयतमानानां पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम् ॥२४॥
दुर्योधनो महाराज व्यगाहत महद्बलनम्। स सन्निपातस्तुमुलस्तेषां तस्य च भारत ॥२५॥

अभवत्सर्वभूतानामभावकरणो महान्।
              धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              तथा यातेषु सैन्येषु तथा कृच्छ्रगतः स्वयम् ॥२६॥
कच्चिद्दुर्योधनः सूत नाकार्षीत्पृष्ठतो रणम्। एकस्य च बहूनां च सन्निपातो महाहवे ॥२७॥
verses.english: Dhritarastra said When the Pandava host was thus advancing and when he was involved in great danger, I hope, O son of a charioteer, Duryodhana did not turn his back on the field of battle.

verses.sanskrit: विशेषतो नरपतेर्विषमः प्रतिभाति मे। सोत्यन्तसुखसंवृद्धो लक्ष्म्या लोकस्य चेश्वरः ॥२८॥
verses.english: That battle between the one and the many, that one again being a king by birth, seems to me to be very unfair.

verses.sanskrit:
एको बहून्समासाद्य कच्चिन्नासीत्पराङ्मुखः।
              सञ्जय उवाच।
              राजन्संग्राममाश्चर्यं तव पुत्रस्य भारत ॥२९॥
verses.english: Brought up in great luxury, attended with great prosperity and the ruler of the worlds, that single-handed son of mine, I hope, did not turn his face away from the field of battle, encountering odds in battle.

verses.sanskrit: एकस्य बहुभिः सार्धं शृणुष्व गदतो मम। दुर्योधनेन समरे पृतना पाण्डवी रणे ॥३०॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said The battle, O king, that was then fought, between your son on the one side and the numerous Pandavas on the other, was indeed wonderful. Hear me as I relate it.

verses.sanskrit: नलिनी द्विरदेनेव समन्तात्प्रतिलोडिता। ततस्तां प्रहितां सेनां दृष्ट्वा पुत्रेण ते नृप ॥३१॥
verses.english: Then the Pandava troops were completely crushed by Duryodhana like a forest of lotuses destroyed by an elephant.

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनपुरोगास्तं पञ्चालाः समुपाद्रवन्। स भीमसेनं दशभिः शरैर्विव्याध पाण्डवम् ॥३२॥
verses.english: Then, o king, beholding the troops shattered by your son, the Panchalas headed by Bhimasena, rushed upon Duryodhana.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिभिस्त्रिभिर्यमौ वीरौ धर्मराजं च सप्तभिः। विराटद्रुपदौ षड्भिः शतेन च शिखण्डिनम्व् ॥३३॥
verses.english: Thereupon your son pierced Bhimasena, the son of Pandu, with ten shafts and each of the twins Nakula and Sahadeva with three and the virtuous king Yudhishthira with seven.

verses.sanskrit: धृष्टद्युम्नं च विंशत्या द्रौपदेयांस्त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः। शतशश्चापरान्योधान्सद्विपांश्च रथान् रणे ॥३४॥
verses.english: He then cut-off many other warriors hundreds in number and elephants and cars in

verses.sanskrit: शरैरवचकर्तोग्रैः क्रुद्धोऽन्तक इव प्रजाः। न सन्दधन्विमुञ्चन्वा मण्डलीकृतकार्मुकः ॥३५॥
अदृश्यत रिपून्निघ्नञ्छिक्षयाऽस्त्रबलेन च। तस्य तान्निघ्नतः शत्रून्हेमपृष्ठं महद्धनुः ॥३६॥
verses.english: Owing to his skill acquired through practies and to the powers of his weapons, he appeared, when striking down his foes, to wield his bow, continuously drawn to a circle whether when aiming or discharging his shafts.

verses.sanskrit: अजस्रं मण्डलीभूतं ददृशुः समरे जनाः। ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा भल्लाभ्यामच्छिनद्धनुः ॥३७॥
verses.english: Then men beheld his mighty bow of golden staff, as he slew his foes, to be always drawn to a circle.

verses.sanskrit: तव पुत्रस्य कौरव्य यतमानस्य संयुगे। विव्याध चैनं दशभिः सम्यगस्तैः शरोत्तमैः ॥३८॥
verses.english: Thereafter king Yudhishthira cut-off with a Pair of Vallas the bow of your son, who had been exerting to the best of his prowess in battle, O foremost of the Kurus.

verses.sanskrit: वर्म चाशु समासाद्य ते भित्त्वा क्षितिमाविशन्। ततः प्रमुदिताः पार्थाः परिवव्रुर्युधिष्ठिरम् ॥३९॥
verses.english: He then pierced the latter with ten excellent shafts all well-directed. But striking against Duryodhana's armour they were shattered into pierces and fell down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit: यथा वृत्रवधे देवाः पुरा शक्रं महर्षयः। ततोऽन्यद्धनुरादाय तव पुत्रः प्रतापवान् ॥४०॥
verses.english: Then the Parthas filled with delight surrounded Yudhishthira, like the celestials and the sages surrounding Shakra on the occasion of the slaughter of Vritra.

verses.sanskrit: तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति राजानं ब्रुवन्पाण्डवमभ्ययात्। तमायान्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य तव पुत्रं महामृधे ॥४१॥
verses.english: Then beholding your son rush to battle with fury, the Panchalas always intent on securing victory received him with delight. son

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्युद्ययुः समुदिताः पञ्चाला जयगृद्धिनः। तान्द्रोणः प्रतिजग्राह परीप्सन् युधि पाण्डवम् ॥४२॥
चण्डवातोद्धुतान्मेघान् गिरिरम्बुमुचो यथा। तत्र राजन्महानासीत्संग्रामो लोमहर्षणः ॥४३॥
verses.english: Drona then encountered that division of the Panchalas, from a desire for rescuring the king, like a mountain with slanting masses of raincharged clouds driven by the tempest.

verses.sanskrit: पाण्डवानां महाबाहो तावकानां च संयुगे। रुद्रस्याक्रीडसदृशः संहारः सर्वदेहिनाम् ॥४४॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O king, there commenced a awful combat making the hair stand erect between the Pandavas and your troops, O mighty-armed one.

verses.sanskrit: ततः शब्दो महानासीत्पुनर्येन धनञ्जयः। अतीव सर्वशब्देभ्यो लोमहर्षकरः प्रभो ॥४५॥
verses.english: The carnage was terrible like that when Rudra slays in sport all creatures at the end of a Yuga. Then arose a loud uproar the place where Dhananjaya was.

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुनस्य महाबाहो तावकानां च धन्विनाम्। मध्ये भारतसैन्यस्य माधवस्य महारणे ॥४६॥
द्रोणस्यापि परैः सार्धं व्यूहद्वारे महारणे। एवमेष क्षयो वृत्तः पृथिव्यां पृथिवीपते। क्रुद्धेऽर्जुने तथा द्रोणे सात्वते च महारथे ॥४७॥
verses.english: Thus continued that dreadful destruction of creatures when, O ruler of men, Arjuna, Drona and the mighty car-warrior Satyaki were excited with wrath.
